Underwriting workbench, CAM and human decisions

A source-linked technical walkthrough. Trace the flow, explain the boundary, then test the failure path.

After this session, you can:
  • Assemble a credit assessment
  • Separate policy outcome from human authority
  • Govern exceptions and overrides

Technical flow

Every hand-off is a control boundary: on failure the flow holds, refers or denies — it never skips ahead.

  1. 01Verified credit facts
  2. 02Policy evaluation
  3. 03CAM proposal
  4. 04Referral / exception
  5. 05Independent approval
  6. 06Decision evidence

1. One evidence map

Applicant, bureau, Account Aggregator, income, obligation, fraud, collateral and product-policy facts retain source and freshness in the credit assessment memorandum.

2. Decision layers

Deterministic policy produces eligibility and referral reasons. Approved models may contribute tagged facts; the sanctioned human authority owns material judgment and cannot delegate approval to generated narrative.

3. Exceptions are explicit

Policy exceptions name the rule, rationale, compensating controls, approver and expiry. Maker-checker and committee independence are validated from authenticated actors and prior action history.
